new_text_review.NEW-TRAP (1.2 + 4.3 + 5.2/5.3 + 6.1): Definitional chain: a recording is one sensor's share at a station (1.2); a station's magnitude is the mean of the channel magnitudes of its readings (4.3), so readings are pooled across both of the station's recordings as one flat mean (not a mean of per-sensor means); the report has one object per recording, and each carries the station magnitude (6.1), so both rows of a two-sensor station show the same ml; the median and the fewer-than-three rule count stations, not recordings (5.2, 5.3). Shipped bulletin.py collects one ml per recording row, so the natural fix double-counts a station in the median and in the count. I find it decidable. Every term is defined, 1.2 guarantees equal epi_km (so both rows share distance and contributes), and the coverage paragraph names the input shape. Two careful readers should agree. The contrary expert habit of treating each sensor stream as its own station is overruled by 1.2's explicit 'at a station' and 'a station has one or two recordings'.
ambiguity_check: Pooled flat mean vs mean of per-recording means: 4.3's 'mean of the channel magnitudes of its readings' is flat. Determined.
Is a two-sensor station's contributes/distance possibly split? No: 1.2 fixes equal epi_km and depth is per event. Determined.
Could the silence clause be read as keeping shipped per-recording behaviour? No: NPM-4 governs station magnitude (4.3) and the median (5.2), so it is not a value without a rule. Determined.
1.2 now allows one or two amplitudes per recording, and up to two recordings per station, giving one to four channels per station, consistent with the instruction's 'one to four horizontal channels'.
1.1 'one to forty recordings' remains compatible with up to two per station.
Report order: rows per recording in file order, duplicate codes allowed, exact comparison of `code` works. Determined.
Recordings of one station need not be adjacent; nothing depends on adjacency. Determined.

solver_path_screen.pre_mortem: The solver maps NPM-4 rules to modules as before and repairs gain, halving, readings, hypocentral distance, linear interpolation, correction sign, mean, median and the fewer-than-three rule. It writes a reference from the manual and differential-tests with self-generated bulletins. Two places escape that loop. (1) If it edits minus_log_a0 to linear, extrapolation turns linear too, and a reference written from 3.3 agrees. The explicit silence sentence in 3.2 now makes it more likely a careful solver keeps the log extrapolation. (2) If it reads the report's 'one object per recording' as per-recording magnitudes, it keeps bulletin.py's per-row counting, so a two-sensor station is double-counted in the median and the three-station count. Its own fuzzer, built on the same reading and on a sample that no longer contains a two-sensor station, will not flag this. The coverage-paragraph mention and the 1.2 definition make trap 2 findable, so Opus 5.5 locally will probably get both. Platform Opus 5 has two independent chances to miss.
solver_path_screen.decisive_reason: Two independent traps of different kinds now sit where self-built references share the solver's reading: a silent-region preservation inside the interpolation function, and a recording-vs-station pooling inside the median/count aggregate. Both are fair by definitional chain, but each is easy to miss when fixing the obvious departure.
